feature1.prompt: Allow to customize the code attribute of ValidationError raised by BaseConstraint.validate. It is currently possible to customize the violation_error_message of a ValidationError raised by a constraint but not the code. The goal is to add a new parameter to BaseConstraint so that a descriptive error code can be provided when raising a ValidationError, eliminating the need to subclass the constraint to tweak its behavior. This change follows Django’s recommendation to supply a descriptive error code when raising a ValidationError.
feature1.hint_texts: This part includes the core logic changes. It involves adding the new violation_error_code parameter to BaseConstraint and propagating it through its subclasses (CheckConstraint, UniqueConstraint, ExclusionConstraint). Updates must be made to the __init__, deconstruct, __eq__, __repr__, and validate methods so that the new parameter is correctly stored and used when a constraint violation occurs. The implementation should ensure that, when a constraint is violated, a ValidationError is raised with the code attribute matching the provided violation_error_code.
feature1.entrypoint: Modify django/db/models/constraints.py and django/contrib/postgres/constraints.py. In django/db/models/constraints.py update the BaseConstraint.__init__ to accept violation_error_code, adjust the deconstruct method to include it, and update __eq__ and __repr__ to compare and display the value. Similarly, update CheckConstraint.__init__, CheckConstraint.__repr__, and CheckConstraint.validate (as well as the analogous methods for UniqueConstraint and ExclusionConstraint) to propagate the new parameter. The starting point is the BaseConstraint class and its subclasses where the parameter is integrated into the super() calls and ValidationError is raised with code set to violation_error_code.

feature2.prompt: Allow to customize the code attribute of ValidationError raised by BaseConstraint.validate. It is currently possible to customize the violation_error_message of a ValidationError raised by a constraint but not the code. By enabling this customization, constraints will now raise a ValidationError with a descriptive error code, eliminating the need for manual subclassing to adjust error handling. This update ensures that constraints across the system behave consistently in their error reporting as recommended in the Django documentation.
feature2.hint_texts: This part covers the updates to the test suite. It involves modifying and adding test cases to verify that the new violation_error_code parameter is correctly integrated into all constraint types. Tests should check that deconstruction outputs include the new parameter, that equality and representation (__eq__ and __repr__) reflect its value, and that ValidationError is raised with the correct code. The testing effort should cover all aspects of constraint behavior across BaseConstraint, CheckConstraint, UniqueConstraint, and ExclusionConstraint to ensure robust integration.
feature2.entrypoint: Modify the test files in tests/constraints/tests.py and tests/postgres_tests/test_constraints.py. In these files update existing test cases and add new ones that verify the behavior of the violation_error_code parameter. Focus on tests that check the custom error code message, deconstruction including the new parameter, equality comparisons, and representation of constraint instances. New test functions such as test_custom_violation_code_message, test_repr_with_violation_error_code, and test_validate_custom_error should be implemented according to the patch diff.
